$comment: Where a symbol may and may not appear. Replaces substring pins in the
*authority* scripts that matched source text rather than identifiers.
Keyed by the authority the rule belongs to, so failures name their owner.
See docs/adr/0016-modules-as-components-of-one-deployable.md and issue #3898.
The beta booking-engine quote lifecycle, deleted in voyant#4188. Its
routes went earlier; the library surface survived unmounted and was
still reachable as a published type from @voyant-travel/catalog-contracts.
Voyant is beta: nothing here is aliased, deprecated or kept for
compatibility. A quote is now either a Session-bound
`bookingQuoteRecordV1` or a non-binding `offerPreviewResultV1`, both
produced by the SAME `composeRequirements` / `composeQuote` ports.
Pinned by identifier rather than by path because these were library
exports, not route modules: a reintroduction would plausibly land at a
new path, and the empty `onlyIn` lists are default-deny over the whole
of packages/. `packages/catalog/src/booking-engine/quote.ts` and its
test are ALSO listed in retired-paths.json, because a file can come
back carrying different names.
A Booking is created by exactly one durable command: Finance's
booking-create command. Commit is its only cross-module caller, and
everything else — every vertical, every route, every hook — is a client
of that command rather than a second implementation of it. See
issue #3747, which removed the parallel implementations, and #4188.
This was previously guarded by listing the deleted files in
retired-paths.json. A path list fails both ways: it false-positives when
a legitimately different module reuses a retired filename, and it can
never see a NEW file at an unlisted path calling the command directly.
onlyIn is default-deny over identifiers, so both go away.
The allowlists are derived from what the code does today. Widening one
is a decision about who may create a Booking, not a formality.
The absentFrom globs restate what the allowlists already imply: a client
package must never name the command, whatever gets added to an allowlist
later. The empty onlyIn lists are the parallel implementations #3747
deleted, pinned by identifier so they cannot return under a new path.
Converted out of scripts/check-operator-catalog-backend-authority.mjs in
voyant#4188, which asserted these by matching `export function <name>`
in source text. Two of its seven pins named symbols this issue deleted
(`createProductQuoteShapeEnricher`, `applyCatalogTaxToQuoteResult`);
both now live in beta-quote-path-authority's onlyIn:[] instead.
presentIn is a slightly weaker assertion than the substring it replaces:
it requires the identifier to be referenced in the file, not to be
exported as a function declaration from it. That is the right strength
for the rule, which is about which package owns the authority, and it no
longer breaks when the declaration is reformatted or changes shape.
The import-specifier checks in that script (`apps/operator`,
`@voyant-travel/inventory`, `@voyant-travel/commerce` must not be imported
by runtime-support) are NOT identifiers and stay there.
Every Voyant<Domain>Provider is an alias of the one VoyantReactProvider,
so rendering one below the operator admin shell replaces the shell's
{ baseUrl, fetcher } for the whole tree — including the admin Better Auth
realm scoping, which silently 404s every auth-react call. Domain hooks read
the shell's context directly and need no re-provider. See issue #4182.
The retired `booking.contract_document.requested` event, deleted in
voyant#4634. Finance emitted it whenever the operator ticked "Generate
invoice and contract"; nothing in the repository ever subscribed to it,
so the contract half of that checkbox went into the outbox and was
consumed by nobody — while the contract the operator asked for was
silently not produced.
The customer contract is generated by Legal off `booking.confirmed`,
which Finance emits on the same commit and which every other path that
confirms a booking emits too. A second trigger for the same idempotent
operation is the ADR-0007 indirection ADR-0016 rejected, so the request
event is retired rather than given a subscriber.
Pinned twice, because either half can come back alone: the event name
itself as a literal, and the payload-schema identifier a manifest event
declaration must name. Both are empty, which is default-deny over the
whole of packages/ — reintroducing either anywhere fails here rather
than after another silent tenant. Comments are not literals to the AST,
so the incident notes that cite the name by way of explanation stay.
The duplicated Proposals checkout Inquiry bridge is superseded by the
Relationships-owned canonical Inquiry intake and may not return.
Customer Signal keeps inquiry/request_offer as read-compatible legacy
values, but every new write is constrained by the active kind schema.
"anonymous-storefront" is the userId auth mints for a storefront guest.
It means "admitted as a public shopper", not "this person", and it is the
same value for every guest on every deployment.
It is also a non-empty string, so anything doing `if (userId)` or
"resolve the customer for this reference" reads it as a real, stable
identity. voyant#4637: the booking-engine checkout passed it to the
payment processor as the customer reference, which minted ONE Stripe
Customer under it and attached every subsequent guest checkout to that
same record — pooling unrelated shoppers' payment history and pinning the
first shopper's billing email on all of them.
Three files already normalised it away and a fourth did not, which is
what a copied sentinel costs. Pinned to its single definition in
core/env.ts; every consumer goes through `identifiedUserId`.
